blocks.text: Why Slack is the command center for public relations

Public relations work requires constant communication and rapid response times. On a Mac, Slack serves as the primary tool for these interactions. You likely juggle multiple workspaces, client channels, and internal team chats throughout the day. Navigating this volume requires more than just mouse clicks. You need keyboard shortcuts and a way to handle information without losing focus.

Slack version 4.53.x on macOS 14 Sonoma or newer provides a stable environment for these tasks. If you find your app becoming sluggish, navigate to Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart. This simple action often restores speed to your workspace. Keeping your environment clean ensures that you spend less time waiting for the app to load and more time managing your media relations.
Essential keyboard shortcuts for PR pros

items: Command + K: Use the Quick Switcher to jump to any conversation.
Command + /: Open the in-app cheat sheet for a full list of shortcuts.
Shift + Enter: Create a new line in your message without sending it.
Command + B: Apply bold formatting to emphasize key points in your pitch.
Command + ,: Open your preferences to manage notification schedules.

blocks.text: Mastering these shortcuts allows you to move through your day with speed. When you are drafting a response to a journalist, you need to be precise. Using Shift + Enter keeps your draft tidy while you structure your thoughts. Do not rely on your mouse for every action. The keyboard is your fastest path to getting things done.
How to stay focused while monitoring media

PR specialists often face the challenge of constant interruptions. Research shows that 51 percent of PR professionals cite limited time for strategic thinking as their biggest stressor. To combat this, you must manage your Slack notifications. Use the profile menu to set your status or pause notifications entirely when you need to write a press release or analyze campaign data. You can also use the /dnd command to silence alerts for a set period.

If you are working on a high-stakes campaign, use the Mute feature on non-urgent channels. This stops the badges from appearing on your dock icon, allowing you to focus on the channels that matter most at that moment.
blocks.title: Protect your focus

blocks.text: Drafting pitches with voice dictation

Writing is a core daily activity for PR professionals. Instead of typing every word, use the dictation feature on your Mac. Hold the fn key and speak your thoughts directly into the Slack input field. This is particularly useful when you need to get a draft out quickly before a deadline. Lazur can help you dictate clean, formatted text that sounds professional and clear.

Always proofread your dictated text before hitting send. While modern macOS dictation is highly accurate, context matters in PR. Ensure that names, brands, and technical terms are transcribed correctly. Taking ten seconds to review your text is faster than sending a follow-up correction later.
Searching for information in Slack

Finding specific information in a sea of messages is a common struggle. Use search modifiers to narrow your results. For example, use 'from:@name' to find messages from a specific client or 'has:link' to find shared resources. Command + G opens the general search, while Command + F searches the current channel. These modifiers save you from scrolling through hours of chat history.
Using Lazur to guide your Slack workflow

Lazur lives in the notch of your Mac and helps you work smarter. When you are unsure how to perform a task in Slack, hold Option + Command and ask Lazur. It will show you exactly where to look on your screen. This is helpful when you are learning new features or trying to remember where a specific setting is hidden in the menu. Lazur does not click for you, but it points and guides so you can finish the task yourself.
Managing multiple workspaces

Many PR specialists manage multiple Slack workspaces for different clients or agency teams. Use the workspace switcher on the left sidebar to jump between them. If you have many workspaces, keep your most active ones at the top. You can drag and drop them to reorder the list. This keeps your most urgent client work front and center.
Common mistakes to avoid

items: Sending messages to the wrong channel: Check the channel name before you hit enter.
Ignoring thread replies: Always reply in a thread to keep the main channel clean.
Overloading channels with attachments: Use a shared folder for large files instead.
Forgetting to set your status: Let your team know when you are in a meeting.

blocks.text: Moving forward with your PR workflow

Your success in PR depends on how well you manage your time and information. Slack is a powerful tool, but it is only as effective as your habits. By using keyboard shortcuts, managing your notifications, and using voice tools like Lazur, you can regain control of your day. Start by picking one shortcut to learn today. Once you master it, move on to the next. Small changes in your workflow lead to significant gains in your ability to handle the demands of public relations.

faq.question: How do I clear the Slack cache on my Mac?
faq.answer: Go to the menu bar and select Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart. This will restart the app and often resolves performance issues.

faq.question: Can I use voice dictation in Slack?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold the fn key on your Mac to dictate text directly into the Slack message field. Lazur can assist with formatting your dictated thoughts.

faq.question: How do I quickly find a message in Slack?
faq.answer: Use Command + G for general search or Command + F to search the current channel. Use modifiers like 'from:' or 'in:' to filter your results.

faq.question: What is the best way to pause notifications?
faq.answer: Click your profile picture in the bottom left, select Pause notifications, and choose a duration. You can also use the /dnd command in any channel.
